content:
jordan: Heads-up — noticed steady RSS growth on long-context chat sessions (100k+ tokens). Dumped a few heap profiles, looks like KV cache has a ton of tiny free blocks that never get reused. attaching flamegraph link: https://perf.internal/fg/1767894321 :disappointed:
amy: can you paste the allocation histogram? curious about block-size distribution.
jordan: sure — short snippet from pprof:
```
allocated-by-size:
  48B:  1.2M
  512B:  900k
  2KB:  150k
  5KB:  4.1k
  16KB: 800
  >64KB: 10
```
we're seeing tons of ~48B and 512B holes after evictions, allocator rarely coalesces because we use a fixed slab bucket strategy.
amy: that explains fragmentation. our slab buckets are 4KB and 64KB boundaries which don't map well to KV chunk sizes for this model (KV entries often 600B or 3KB depending on layer). small allocations never merge.
ciara: is this the same behaviour we saw in the synthetic paging test last month? we hit high p95 mem when sequence lengths increase and repeated context churn.
jordan: yes similar pattern but worse: with long contexts the KV cache does many partial prefix evictions leaving interleaved free blocks; allocator internal free lists are very fragmented.
raj: perf-bot ran a quick regression check on canary branch (kv/heap-coalesce) — results:
- baseline mem growth (100k tokens): +1.8GB
- coalesce patch: +0.6GB
- p95 latency delta: +1.2% (within SLO)
perf-bot: automated profile attached: https://perf.internal/run/1767894321/summary
amy: interesting — what does the coalesce do? full compaction or only buddy merge on free?
jordan: prototype does local coalescing on free (merge adjacent free blocks within page), plus a new medium-size bucket (2K/8K) to better match KV chunk sizes. no global stop-the-world compaction in this PR.
ciara: any pause concerns? background compactor might be safer than synchronous merges.
ajam: (typo) — meant amy ^
amy: I ran small stress on my laptop — merges are O(n) per page but we bound to N frees per cycle so pause negligible. still, we should avoid doing this inline on hot allocation paths.
raj: can we push compaction to background thread and opportunistic coalesce on free in fast path? prefer non-blocking.
jordan: that's plan B: opportunistic coalesce when free is returned (cheap neighbor checks), and a background sweep every X seconds to coalesce larger holes and move large contiguous KV segments to reduce fragmentation.
perf-bot: micro-bench (local): alloc/free throughput drop ~3% with opportunistic checks; background compactor adds ~0.5% CPU overhead.
amy: tradeoffs look OK. also want instrumentation: histogram of free-run lengths and per-page fragmentation ratio so we can alert once fragmentation > 30%.
ciara: what about block-size tuning? saw spike when we used 4KB base slab. maybe try 2KB base with power-of-two buddy for larger sizes? smaller base reduces internal waste for small KV entries.
jordan: tried 2KB slabs: reduced small waste but increased number of metadata entries and slight CPU overhead. middle ground: introduce 2KB and 8KB buckets (instead of 4KB/64KB) — seems to match distribution in our workloads.
raj: what's the rollout plan? want canary on dedicated and hosted with low % first.
jordan: propose:
1) feature-flagged release with opportunistic coalesce + new buckets
2) canary on Dedicated pool for 2 days (10% traffic)
3) collect mem profiles, fragmentation hist, latency SLOs
4) if green, enable background compactor opt-in for customers with heavy long-context loads
amy: will open PR with docs and toggles today. adding perf dashboards: frag-ratio, free-run-hist, compactor-ops/sec, and p99 mem-growth.
ciara: also add unit tests for boundary merges and a fuzz test that simulates random eviction/alloc patterns for a million ops.
raj: please add an experiment to replay production eviction traces to the test harness — we should match real churn.
jordan: good call — I have traces from last month, will add replay. expected timeline: PR + perf dashboards by EOD tomorrow, canary by Friday if no blocker.
amy: I'll review the PR in the morning. tagging @ciara for fuzz test review.
ciara: will do. thanks everyone. :thumbsup:
